data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** f2f4cea3f85000795619e7a072669e9e23233e42

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

Per follow-on-epic-gate.md, when a follow-on epic at depth 0 lacks sufficient context for a well-formed spec (undefined success criteria, unresolved scope questions, unclear overlap with other epics), brainstorm should either:

(a) Run additional Socratic dialogue to clarify the follow-on scope before drafting SCs and invoking the scrutiny pipeline, OR
(b) Recognize the follow-on is underspecified and create it as a placeholder stub (similar to the depth >= 1 stub path) tagged scrutiny:pending, skipping fidelity review entirely.

The gate at phases/follow-on-epic-gate.md defines the depth 0 full scrutiny path but does not include a readiness check — it assumes the drafted spec will be complete enough to pass fidelity review. When the follow-on originates from a directional user statement (e.g., "design per-story PRs as follow-on epic"), the available context is insufficient to produce a spec that passes fidelity review without additional dialogue.

#### Actual Behavior

Brainstorm drafted a 2-SC follow-on epic from a directional user statement without running any additional dialogue to clarify scope, overlap, or validation strategy. It then dispatched 3 fidelity reviewer sub-agents against the incomplete spec. All three reviewers returned multiple dimensions below 4 (self_contained=2, success_measurable=2, right_sized=2, no_overlap=3, validation_signal=2). The spec was then created as a stub anyway with scrutiny:pending.

The fidelity review was wasted — it consumed 3 sub-agent dispatches to confirm what was already evident: a directional statement without additional dialogue cannot produce a spec that passes scrutiny.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* **Affected skill:** /dso:brainstorm (Phase 3 Step 0 — Follow-on Epic Gate)
* **Affected file:** plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/phases/follow-on-epic-gate.md
* **Related file:** plugins/dso/skills/shared/workflows/epic-scrutiny-pipeline.md (Step 4: Fidelity Review)

### Proposed Fix Direction (not a root cause — per Zero Inference Rule)

Add a readiness gate before dispatching the scrutiny pipeline on follow-on epics at depth 0. Options:

1. Add a "follow-on readiness check" that evaluates whether the drafted spec has enough substance to warrant full scrutiny (e.g., SCs are specific and testable, not placeholder text). If not, route to either additional dialogue or stub creation.
2. Require at least one round of Socratic dialogue for directional follow-ons before invoking the scrutiny pipeline — the same Phase 1 "Tell Me More" loop used for primary epics, but scoped to the follow-on's narrower topic.
3. Add a lightweight pre-flight that checks SC specificity (e.g., no "pending" markers, no undefined terms) before dispatching fidelity reviewers.
data.title: Brainstorm Follow-on Gate: incomplete follow-on epic runs full fidelity review -> wasted scrutiny on unfinished spec
